steps.title: Configure GC-TOF MS General Parameters
steps.instruction: Set the instrument parameters for primary metabolism profiling using the Gerstel Cold Injection system and Agilent 7890A GC with Leco Pegasus III/IV MS.

substeps.instruction: Set Method Name to 'quick_Splitless_ms_alex'.
Configure Injector: Gerstel MPS/CIS, Splitless mode, Purge Time 25 sec, Purge Flow 40mL/min, Injector Vol 0.5µL.
Set Carrier gas to Helium at 1ml/min.
Install Column: RTX-5MS (30m long, 0.25mm i.d., 0.25mm film duraguard with 10m guard to column; Restek #12723-127).
Set MS parameters: Solvent Delay 335 sec, Ion Source Temp 250°C, Scan Rate 17specs/sec, Detector Voltage 1750 V to 1950V.

steps.title: Prepare System for Column Change
steps.instruction: Safely cool and power down the GC-TOF system before replacing the capillary column.

substeps.instruction: Cool oven to 30°C via the Agilent GC front panel.
Cool inlet (CIS temp) to 20°C by loading the 'injector plate change and clean method' in Maestro software.
Turn electrical power OFF using the front instrument switch.
Wait ~1.5 hours until ion source temperature is < 100°C.
Close Maestro and ChromaTOF software.
Turn vacuum OFF using the front instrument switch.
Slowly vent the turbo pump by twisting the vent knob until hissing stops, then close the knob.
Unscrew the pump cable (if not using CORE).
Remove the safety pin and separate the table.
Open the oven door.

steps.title: Install New GC Column
steps.instruction: Install the new Rtx5-Sil column at the injector and detector sites.

substeps.instruction: Remove old column from injector; insert new column ensuring the 'Guard Column End' goes to the injector.
If reusing ferrule or adapter, sonicate in ethyl acetate for 5 minutes.
At detector site: Unscrew the round plate (if applicable) to reveal the transfer line.
Unscrew transfer line nut and pull out the old column.
Remove the grey ferrule from the nut using a paperclip or tack if stuck.
Unwind ~2 feet of new column and insert the grey ferrule and nut.
Cut ~10 cm of the new column and wipe clean with methanol and a Kimwipe.
Feed column through the interface pole with the transfer nut finger-tight, leaving 4-6mm protruding.
Mark the column position on the opposite side of the nut/ferrule using a Sharpie.
Feed column into the actual interface and screw the nut and ferrule VERY TIGHTLY, verifying length via the Sharpie mark.
Screw the round silver cover back into place (if applicable).
Replace the table, insert the safety pin, and close the oven door.
Screw the pump cable back on (if not using CORE).

steps.title: Restore Vacuum and Condition Column
steps.instruction: Re-establish vacuum and perform thermal conditioning of the new column.

substeps.instruction: Turn vacuum ON and open Maestro and ChromaTOF software.
Wait at least 3 hours for vacuum pressure to reach 1E-7.
Turn electrical power ON.
Wait one hour after the transfer line reaches 280°C and ion source reaches 250°C to reduce moisture.
Condition the column twice: 50°C (1 min) → 10°C/min to 100°C (10 min) → 10°C/min to 330°C (20 min).
Adjust CIS temp to 250°C for at least 15 minutes, then bring down to 50°C.
Perform a leak check and condition the column with corn samples and quality controls.

steps.title: Trim Column After Complex Matrix Analysis
steps.instruction: Cut the column to remove contaminants and restore system performance.

substeps.instruction: Cool oven to 30°C and inlet to 20°C (via Maestro 'injector plate change and clean method').
Turn gas saver OFF via the GC front panel.
Open oven door and remove the adapter nut using wrench 'I'.
Remove column by pulling the ferrule. If stuck, remove back adapter using wrench 'G' and pry ferrule off with pliers.
If replacing adapter: Insert septa into column end, remove metal cover, unscrew adapter with wrench 'G', install new adapter (finger-tight), and replace cover.
Measure ~10 cm and cut the column with the Agilent ruler/cutter; verify cut is straight with a magnifying glass.
Clean the column tip with MeOH on a Kimwipe.
Measure 1.7 cm from the front of the ferrule to the column end (if using a new ferrule, tighten it in the injector first to ensure a snug fit before measuring).
Thread column into adapter, push ferrule into place by hand, and screw adapter nut back in.
Position column to avoid touching oven sides and close the door.
Turn gas saver back ON and verify pressure holds.
Increase oven temp to 50°C. If a new ferrule was installed, increase CIS temp to 250°C for 10 mins, then return to 50°C.
Perform leak check at 50°C CIS temp and 7.7psi pressure.

steps.title: Clean and Assemble CIS Liners
steps.instruction: Maintain and assemble the Gerstel CIS injector liners.

substeps.instruction: Remove glass liner from transport adapter and dispose of used liners in broken glass waste.
Unscrew the smaller piece from the larger head using an Allen wrench.
Remove the septa from the smaller piece using a push pin.
Rinse adapter head with isopropanol and scrub with a test tube brush (avoid squirting isopropanol directly on O-rings).
Sonicate the smaller piece in isopropanol for 5 minutes.
Dry all pieces on a Kimwipe.
Insert a new septa and screw the smaller piece back into the adapter head with an Allen wrench.
Use the black assembly tool to attach the adapter to a new glass liner: insert liner (baffled end first), place adapter (septa up), press down firmly, and tug gently to ensure a snug fit.

steps.title: Generate Acquisition Sequence
steps.instruction: Create and synchronize sequence tables across MiniX, ChromaTOF, and Maestro software.

substeps.instruction: In MiniX: Select study, choose instrument (core GC-TOF-a or research GC-TOF-b), check boxes for blanks/QCs, set start date, and select data acquisition settings.
Download the acquisition table and save it to the network drive (jupiter.fiehnlab.ucdavis.edu) in the minix folder using the format: [StudyType]_[Date]_[MiniXID]_[Description].
In ChromaTOF: Load the file via Acquisition Tasks → Sequence Table → Load.
Configure the sequence: Start with 3 liner conditions, reagent blank, and QC6-1. Set samples to start at vial 10 (vial 2 empty).
Insert 3 liner conditions, reagent blank, and QC6 every 10 samples. End study with a single QC6 run.
Note: Tray holds 98 vials; restart numbering at #10 after #98.
Save the modified sequence in the minix folder.
In Maestro: Create a new sequence or use a template. Copy the Vial column from ChromaTOF and paste it into the Maestro Vial column.
Insert a 'NEWLINER' row before every liner conditioning set.
Verify that vial numbers match between ChromaTOF and Maestro using an Excel spreadsheet (excluding NEWLINER positions).
Save the Maestro sequence to C:\Program files\Maestro\1\Sequence using the same name as the ChromaTOF file.
